div.head: VIII Atr 6
div.ab: And be teoðunge se cyng ⁊ his witan habbað gecoren ⁊ gecweden, ealswa hit riht is, þæt ðriddan dæl þare teoðunge, þe to circan gebyrge, ga to ciricbote ⁊ oðer dæl þam Godes þeowum, þridde Godes þearfum ⁊ earman þeowetlingan.

And be teoðunge se cyng ⁊ his witan habbað gecoren ⁊ gecweden, ealswa hit riht is, þæt ðriddan dæl þare teoðunge þe to circan gebyrge ga to ciricbote ⁊ oðer dæl þam Godes þeowum, þridde Godes þearfum ⁊ earman þeowetlingan.

And be teoðunge, se cyng and his witan habbað gecoren and gecweden, ealswa hit riht is, þæt ðriddan dæl þare teoðunge, þe to circan gebyrge, ga to ciricbote, and oðer dæl þam Godes þeowum, þridde Godes þearfum and earman þeowetlingan.

Und über den Zehnt haben der König und seine Witan entschieden und bestimmt, wie es recht ist, dass der dritte Theil des Zehnten, welcher der Kirche zukommt, der Kirchenausbesserung zugehe und das zweite Drittel den Gottesdienern, das dritte Gottes Elenden und armen Knechten.

And concerning tithe, the king and his witan have chosen and declared, as is right, that a third part of the tithe that belongs to the church go to the repair of the church, and the second [third] to the servants of God, the third to God's poor and needy slaves.

And with regard to tithes, the king and his councillors have decided and agreed, in accordance with the principles of justice, that a third part of the tithes which belong to the church shall be assigned to the repair of churches, the second portion to the servants of God, and the third portion to God’s poor and to poverty-stricken slaves.

And with reference to tithing, the king and his councilors have decided and decreed, just as is right, that a one-third portion of the tithes belonging to the Church are to go to the upkeep of the church, and another portion to God’s servants, and one-third to God’s poor and impoverished slaves.

Liebermann notes that D treats texts arbitrarily (abridging, adding, altering and mixing), so the external authority for what follows, which G does not lack merely by chance, is slight; but c. 43 was written after Edward II was forgotten and before 1016, and Cnut used other chapters.

note.seg: D behandelt Texte willkürlich; kürzt, vermehrt, ändert und mengt (vgl. oben S. 146*. 245*. 252, Sp. 2*. 254³·⁵. 256, Sp. 2*). Die äussere Beglaubigung des Folgenden, das G nicht bloss zufällig fehlt (vgl. S. 263, Sp. 2¹), ist also gering. [Doch entstand c. 43, nachdem Eadweard II vergessen war, aber vor 1016; und andere Capitel benutzt Cnut.]

D treats texts arbitrarily: it abridges, adds, alters and mixes (cf. above p. 146*. 245*. 252, col. 2*. 254³·⁵. 256, col. 2*). The external authentication of what follows, which is missing in G not merely by chance (cf. p. 263, col. 2¹), is therefore slight. [However, c. 43 arose after Eadweard II had been forgotten, but before 1016; and other chapters are used by Cnut.]

Vgl. Gl Kirchengeldverwendung 4; Zehnt 9ff.; Armenpflege 7ff. Selborn hält die Dreiteilung für nie praktisch geworden, unter Æthelred allein fremdher eingedrängt, von Cnut verworfen; Anc. facts 373. Ein Ggsatz gegen II Eg 2ff. = I Cn 11 liegt nicht notwendig in dieser Dreiteilung, die D in VIIa Atr 2, 3 vielleicht hierher entnahm. Bei Papst Gelasius a. 492—96 schon zeigt sie Bright Church hist. 56

Cf. Gl Kirchengeldverwendung 4; Zehnt 9ff.; Armenpflege 7ff. Selborn holds that the tripartite division never became practice, was imposed from abroad under Æthelred alone, and was rejected by Cnut; Anc. facts 373. This tripartite division, which D perhaps took over into this place from VIIa Atr 2, 3, does not necessarily imply a contradiction of II Eg 2ff. = I Cn 11. Bright Church hist. 56 shows it already under Pope Gelasius a. 492—96
